- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 88+ → 89+), then sharply correct downward.
- Mean reversion is strong in the final 5–10 days of the forecast; model fails to reflect this, often holding high values.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to recent price drops; underestimates downward momentum.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 10 days, then become overly pessimistic in the last 10 days.
- Model fails to capture the “volatility clustering” effect — overestimates calm periods and underestimates sudden drops.
- When history shows a clear downward trend, model often fails to adjust forecast mean downward sufficiently.
- Model tends to smooth out short-term volatility, leading to underestimation of sharp reversals.
- Forecasts are often too high in the middle of the horizon (days 15–25) when true price is trending downward.
- Model exhibits “peak-prediction bias” — overestimates peak prices and underestimates troughs.
